source_read: PMC record PMC12989908 (abstract and references only; it links to Bookshelf), then the full text on NCBI Bookshelf NBK621252 (National Vital Statistics Reports 75(1):1-13, 5 March 2026), read in the app's browser in my own tab: all sections; Table A, the rates Table, Table B and Table C, each read as text on its own Bookshelf page; and the legends and notes of Figures 1 to 4 on their own pages. The figure plots duplicate the rates Table, so no values were read from images. The supplementary spreadsheet of search terms (Table.xlsx, a download) was not opened. Card check only (the task lists no claims). I read the report and noted my own observations before opening the card. By script I recomputed all 105 Table A percentages, all 30 Table B and 30 Table C percentages, the text percentages and changes, and the card's sums and ratios. The section structure was checked with a script for the paragraph locators.

key_findings.correction: All at the stated place. In 2023 the undetermined share was 2,926 of 106,352 = 2.75%, inside the stated 3% to 5% only after rounding.
Paragraphs 1 to 5 of that subsection as stated (the precursor example given is depropionylfentanyl).
Recomputed: the 15 counts sum to 103,675 in 2017 (1.466 times 70,715) and 179,965 in 2023 (1.692 times 106,352).

Locator note: Data considerations has, in order, three running-text paragraphs, a bulleted list, then two more paragraphs. The card counts the list as a paragraph, so the 'minimum number or rate' sentence is its 5th. If lists are not counted (running text only), it is the 4th, and the rare-drugs sentence is the 5th rather than the 6th.
All seven yearly percentages and the three statements on how reporting may affect trends match. The Results write T36.0-T50.8; the Table A note writes T36-T50.8.
Content matches. Same locator note as finding 5: the rare-drugs sentence is the 6th paragraph only if the bulleted list is counted.
Every count, percentage and rank matches Table A and the Results bullets; 108,790 / 70,715 = +53.8%.
Every rate matches the rates Table, and the annual percent changes match the Results. The note is right: Table footnote 4 and the Figure 2 legend both give p < 0.05 for the 2022-to-2023 fall.

Fentanyl is the most frequent concomitant drug for all 9 other top-10 drugs. Every Table B percentage reproduces from its counts, with all deaths involving the referent drug as denominator (6,033/6,096 = 99.0%; 2,002/4,142 = 48.3%; 24,084/31,700 = 76.0%; 22,705/34,167 = 66.5%).
Every Table C percentage reproduces with all deaths of each intent as denominator.

reporting_issues.note: Re-found independently: Table footnote 4 and the Figure 2 legend give p < 0.05 for the 2023 rate being lower than 2022, against 'not statistically significant' in the Discussion.
Hydrocodone 0.9 to 0.6 and diazepam 0.7 to 0.5 match the Table; (1.2 - 1.9)/1.9 = -36.8%.

Re-found independently. The notes to the rates Table and to Figures 1 to 4 (Figure 4 as well as 1 to 3) say 'at least one specific drug in the literal text'. The Table A note says 'specific drug or drug class', identified by T36-T50.8 codes, and the Methods define the measure by T-codes.
Re-found independently: the Table C groups sum to 106,352 with the 218 homicides, and the Table B denominators are the Table A totals.

Figure 3 legend: rates for 2017-2020 do not meet the standard of 'more than 20 deaths'. Figure 2 legend: '20 or more'. Analysis and Table: fewer than 20 not shown. Bromazolam in the Table: no data 2017-2019, fewer than 10 in 2020.

risk_of_bias.note: The editors' evidence-report checklist read as a statistics report, with an overall 'some concerns', fits. The tables are internally consistent (I reproduced every percentage in Tables A, B and C), and the problems are in the Discussion's wording and the notes, as the card says. The card never turns 'mentioned' or 'involved' into 'caused'.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor. The abstract's 'stabilized' for a 1.8% fall (22.7 to 22.3) that the Table calls significant is a fair lay summary; the substantive conflicts are inside the Discussion and are all listed.

missed: Discussion › Findings for specific drugs, 3rd paragraph, lists methamphetamine among drugs with steep increases from 2017 to 2023. The Results and Table footnote 6 give a significant increase only for 2017-2021, with the rate stable from 2021 (9.7) to 2023 (10.4). This is a sixth example of the Discussion going beyond its tables, in the same paragraph as gaps 1 to 3.

Results › Drug overdose deaths in 2023 involving multiple drugs, 2nd paragraph, calls methamphetamine the second or third most frequent concomitant drug 'among the other top drugs'. For oxycodone, Table B gives alprazolam (19.1%) and cocaine (17.2%) as second and third, so methamphetamine is not in the top three for every drug. Minor.

Locator consistency (findings 5 and 7, and the interpretation gap's 'Data considerations, 5th and 6th paragraphs'): these numbers count the bulleted list as a paragraph. Running-text-only counting gives 4th and 5th. Worth fixing one way for all readers' anchors.
